fields.label: What must the proposed specification change?

risks.mitigation: Add read-store.ts and observation.ts to T1 and require the assessor to trace parsing, committed read, ordered event selection, mapping, and acknowledgement.
risks.description: Restricting T1 evidence to its two named paths can yield a formally incomplete assessment of ordering and exact committed-config loading.

risks.mitigation: Permit dependency materialization only via bun install --frozen-lockfile when needed, verify tracked status remains clean, and report inability to install rather than changing dependency metadata.
risks.description: A non-frozen bun install may change the tracked lockfile or otherwise dirty an audit worktree despite the no-edit requirement.

risks.mitigation: Keep the existing known-issue rule: run the command once, preserve exact output and exit status/counts, and never infer or invent passing results.
risks.description: Observation integration tests depend on database/runtime prerequisites and may be unable to execute in the builder environment.

body.summary: Implementable audit with no blocker or operator decision. PR #791 is open as a draft against epic/grade-pray, and its head branch and SHA match the locally available audit target c7e326b7d1c7b03e8d051a079967d496b07e541f. The committed code supports T1 default-off launch grading and T2 exact-claim fenced, atomic completion. Two specification warnings should be corrected before planning: T1 names only parsing/mapping files although ordered delivery is implemented in two additional files, and the conditional dependency install should be frozen so it cannot conflict with the no-file-edits rule. No tests were run during analysis.

findings.description: T1 is grounded in the committed model: RunConfig names grading_enabled, parseRunConfig defaults an absent value to false, rejects non-booleans, and returns the normalized choice (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts:7-11,21-41). Dedicated tests cover missing, explicit, and malformed values (oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-84).

T1 under-specifies the evidence surface for its phrase through the ordered launch delivery. observation-mapping.ts only maps a CommittedRunConfig supplied by its caller (oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts:14-18,42-48); the exact committed config is loaded in oakridge-dbos/src/storage/read-store.ts:467-476 and joined to the ordered launched event in oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation.ts:13-20,33-45. Add those paths to T1 so the assessor can substantiate the full claim rather than only parsing and final mapping.

T2 exact-current-claim fencing is present and independently observable: the predicate requires claimed status, matching lease owner and attempt, and an unexpired lease; settlement locks first, rechecks after the lock, and fences the authoritative update again (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:194-228). The worker passes the same ExecutionClaim through request marking and settlement (observation/src/grading/worker.ts:71-90).

T2 atomic completion is explicitly one transaction: completeExecution settles the execution, closes the matching provider attempt, inserts grade_observation, and returns completion inside one withTenant transaction (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:267-292). The integration test demonstrates both-commit-or-neither behavior by forcing an invalid observation insert and observing neither completion nor answer before a valid retry (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:231-244); separate tests exercise expired, reclaimed, and lock-wait-stale claims (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:304-357).

The builder is told both not to edit files and to run bun install if needed. The repository has a tracked bun.lock and a Bun workspace (package.json:7-11), while observation exposes the requested full-suite test script (observation/package.json:6-8). Clarify that dependency installation must use the frozen lockfile and must not alter tracked files; otherwise a routine install can violate the audit-only constraint even though no source edit was intended.

requirements.description: Produce exactly one cohort named audit with exactly tasks T1 and T2, while retaining at least three distinct analysis findings.
T1 verifies that grading_enabled is carried in run launch config, defaults off when absent, and reaches ordered launch delivery.
T2 verifies that evaluation settlement is fenced to the exact current claim and completion appends its observation atomically.

Builder performs a read-only audit of the pinned PR head, runs the observation test command once, reports actual output/counts, and publishes the existing PR without source edits, commits, pushes, PR mutation, merge, database reset, or deployment.
Assessor evaluates the same commit, supplies at least one path:line-range finding per task, cites test/output evidence separately, and reports the builder run as test_evidence.

source_spec_refs: Audit scope: isolated verification of PR #791 with exactly one audit cohort and two tasks
T1: grading_enabled launch config, default off, through ordered launch delivery
T2: exact-current-claim settlement fencing and transactional observation append
Builder constraints: checkout pinned head, no repository/PR/deployment mutation, one observation test run, publish existing PR
Assessor evidence: same commit, one finding per task, path ranges plus separate test/output evidence

proposed_spec_updates.change: After the two existing T1 paths, add oakridge-dbos/src/storage/read-store.ts and oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation.ts, and say the audit must trace the normalized config from committed run storage into the cursor-ordered launched delivery before mapping.
proposed_spec_updates.reason: The listed run-config and mapping files establish normalization and output shape, but the additional files implement exact committed-config loading and ordered delivery, which are necessary to verify the full requirement.

proposed_spec_updates.change: Replace bun install if needed with bun install --frozen-lockfile if dependencies are missing, require the builder to confirm no tracked file changed, and require reporting the install as unable rather than modifying dependency metadata.
proposed_spec_updates.reason: This makes dependency preparation compatible with the explicit no-file-edits audit constraint and the tracked Bun lockfile.
